prize_parts.citation: for dynamical mean-field theory of strongly correlated electrons

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged. B048 identifies a clean and general physical construction: the controlled infinite-coordination limit and its dynamical self-consistent formulation made local electronic correlations tractable in a way that has become a durable common language of correlated-electron physics. Its value is not solely computational convenience; it exposed an organizing mechanism that can be tested, extended, and confronted with materials experiments. Vollhardt, Georges, and Kotliar represent the essential route from controlled limit to usable dynamical framework within the three-person constraint.
statement.case_against: The framework is not an exact solution for finite-dimensional materials, and its subsequent development includes important extensions and a broad community. The proposed award must therefore be confined to the founding dynamical mean-field construction, without claiming a complete theory of correlated materials. The sequential intellectual history also requires a focused documentary review to confirm that the three credited names fairly capture the indispensable foundational contributions.

responses.point: Eriksson supports B048 as a transformative, experimentally connected framework for correlated-electron physics, while emphasizing that the division of foundational credit needs scrutiny.
responses.response: I agree. The decisive strength is the conjunction of a controlled theoretical idea with consequences that survived comparison across many material systems; this distinguishes a general mechanism from a merely elegant formalism. I also agree that attribution is the limiting issue, so my continued support is conditional on historical confirmation that the Vollhardt, Georges, and Kotliar sequence can be stated without effacing comparably indispensable work.

responses.point: Kroll argues that B045 has a sharply identifiable magic-wavelength principle, exceptional reproducibility, and unusually compact attribution to Katori and Ye.
responses.response: This makes B045 my leading alternative. The magic-wavelength idea is a genuine physical solution to a systematic limitation, rather than simply a performance record. I retain B048 because its conceptual framework reorganized an entire difficult class of many-body problems and its scientific consequences do not depend on a future technological trajectory; nevertheless, B045 would be preferable if the historical review finds the DMFT three-person attribution materially incomplete.

responses.point: Lindroth favors B019 because optical lattices made interacting many-body Hamiltonians controllable, but acknowledges that the foundational achievement exceeds any simple three-person allocation.
responses.response: I share the admiration for the direct, transparent relation between engineered Hamiltonians and observable collective physics. That same breadth is why I continue to place it below B048: the proposed B019 trio is necessarily selective across several theoretical and experimental stages, whereas DMFT can be bounded more closely around one theoretical construction and its formulation.

uncertainties: Whether documentary historical review confirms that Vollhardt, Georges, and Kotliar alone fairly delimit the foundational development of dynamical mean-field theory.
How to word the citation so that it recognizes the original dynamical mean-field construction rather than its later cluster, computational, and materials-specific extensions.
Whether the magic-wavelength lattice-clock principle provides a more secure final attribution if the DMFT historical division of credit proves insufficiently bounded.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with the proposed laureates is apparent from the supplied profile. I share the Gothenburg physics environment with Göran Johansson and Eva Olsson, but no specific collaboration or candidate connection is indicated.
